title: Embed & Rerank Field Suppression, Audit Schema, and Retention Tiers
creator: Liam Chen
description: Design and implement a production-ready logging and retention model for embeddings and rerank endpoints that minimizes sensitive-data exposure while preserving the telemetry needed for debugging, quality tracking, and billing. This ticket covers: 1) field-level suppression rules (deterministic and ML-backed), 2) a compact append-only audit event schema for compliance, 3) retention tiering (short/medium/long) with encryption-at-rest and KMS integration, 4) runtime controls per-tenant (sampling, hashed-logs, suppression on/off), and 5) perf guardrails to keep median tail latency impact <5% under typical batching scenarios. The implementation must support a gradual canary rollout and a quick rollback path.
acceptance_criteria: Field suppression pipeline in front of long-term logs: configurable regex blacklist + ML PII classifier enabled by default for public tenants
Append-only audit events emitted for rerank/embedding calls that contain no raw PII fields in long-term storage (short-term debug buffer allowed), schema v1.0-draft validated by security
Retention tiers implemented: 7 days (debug buffer), 90 days (operational), 7 years (audit locked) with KMS-wrapped keys per-customer for long-term retention
Runtime flags per-tenant: sampling_rate, hashed_logging_mode, redact_mode (none/partial/full) exposed via Console and API
End-to-end e2e test demonstrating <5% median latency increase for 1024-token average requests when suppression + hashing is enabled at 50% sampling
Documentation and runbook for on-call: how to enable debug buffer, request audit exports, and perform retention-era log deletion
tasks: Spec audit_event schema and field whitelist/blacklist (security review)
Implement suppression middleware in embeddings/rerank proxy (regex -> ML classifier -> deterministic scrubbing)
Add hashed-logging mode (HMAC token-level) and integrate with KMS for per-tenant keys
Retention pipeline: short-term debug buffer (S3 encrypted, TTL 7d), operational store (90d), and locked archive (7y) with export hooks
Console UI: per-tenant toggles for sampling_rate and redact_mode + observability panel
Perf testing harness and benchmark suite: microbenchmarks + end-to-end load tests
Create PR with feature flags and rollout plan; coordinate with infra for capacity and SLO adjustments
notes: Trade-offs considered: full in-flight redaction reduces operational visibility; we opted for a short encrypted debug buffer (7 days) that is access-controlled for SREs.
ML-backed PII detector gives better recall than regex for free-text, but adds ~0.8ms median overhead per request; thus classifier runs behind sampling and only on sampled traces by default.
Hashing vs. redaction: hashing preserves ability to detect repeated identifiers across requests without storing raw values. Use HMAC with per-tenant KMS key to avoid cross-tenant correlation risks.
We will not change user-facing APIs; this is a server-side logging and retention enhancement only.
Security sign-off required before enabling long-term archive for regulated customers.

perf_estimates: HMAC token hashing median: 0.6ms; can be offloaded to crypto accel on Dedicated pools
Expected median end-to-end latency delta: +3-5% at 50% sampling with batching preserved
Throughput impact: negligible (<2%) at typical rbatches=16, measurable CPU pressure on small instances under rbatches>64
retention_policy_summary: Short-term debug buffer: 7d (encrypted, access-controlled). Operational logs: 90d (indexed, redact/hashed). Audit archive: 7y (write-once, KMS-wrapped keys, legal hold support). Customers can request export; deletion requests for long-term archive require governance workflow.
rollback_plan: Disable canary flag (0% traffic), allow debug buffer to expire, and run backfill scrub job to remove any disputed entries. Ops runbook includes script to rotate per-tenant keys and revoke archive access. Immediate customer notifications for regulated tenants.
open_questions: Should ML PII detector model be updated centrally or allow per-customer tunable model thresholds? (Security prefers central control to avoid drift)
What encryption key-rotation cadence do we expose to customers? Default 90 days or customer-managed schedule?
How granular must audit events be for SOC2 auditors vs. what we store for debugging?
